classification.difficultyReason: Sketch shifted cubic power curves, including reversed factors and an external negative, using triple roots, intercepts and leading signs.

content.prompt: Sketch the graph of the following.

answer.short: Increasing cubic with a horizontal point of inflection at $(-1,0)$ and $y$-intercept $(0,1)$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x+1&=0\\x&=-1\\f(0)&=(0+1)^3\\f(0)&=1\end{align*}$$

The root $x=-1$ is triple. The coefficient of $x^3$ is positive, so the graph rises from left to right. It crosses the $x$-axis horizontally at $(-1,0)$ and passes through $(0,1)$.

answer.short: Decreasing cubic with a horizontal point of inflection at $(1,0)$ and $y$-intercept $(0,1)$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x-1&=0\\x&=1\\f(0)&=-(0-1)^3\\f(0)&=1\end{align*}$$

The root $x=1$ is triple. The coefficient of $x^3$ is negative, so the graph falls from left to right. It crosses the $x$-axis horizontally at $(1,0)$ and passes through $(0,1)$.

answer.short:
Decreasing cubic with a horizontal point of inflection at $(3,0)$ and $y$-intercept $(0,27)$.

Use $(3-x)^3=-(x-3)^3$ to identify the negative leading coefficient.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}3-x&=0\\x&=3\\f(0)&=(3-0)^3\\f(0)&=27\end{align*}$$

The root $x=3$ is triple. Since $(3-x)^3=-(x-3)^3$, the coefficient of $x^3$ is negative. Draw a decreasing cubic through $(0,27)$, crossing the $x$-axis horizontally at $(3,0)$.

answer.short:
Increasing cubic with a horizontal point of inflection at $(2,0)$ and $y$-intercept $(0,-8)$.

Use $-(2-x)^3=(x-2)^3$ to identify the positive leading coefficient.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2-x&=0\\x&=2\\f(0)&=-(2-0)^3\\f(0)&=-8\end{align*}$$

The root $x=2$ is triple. Since $-(2-x)^3=(x-2)^3$, the coefficient of $x^3$ is positive. Draw an increasing cubic through $(0,-8)$, crossing the $x$-axis horizontally at $(2,0)$.
